case.title: Pastor Akpan Samuel Effiong v. Department of State Service
defendants: Department of State Service (The State Security Services Abuja)

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Claimant instituted action via Amended Complaint with accompanying frontloaded documents filed on 5th June, 2014 against the defendants.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: The suit was originally commenced in the Federal High Court Uyo on 9th December 2010 and later transferred to the National Industrial Court, Calabar Judicial Division.
procedural_events: Claimant filed Amended Complaint on 5th June 2014.
Defendant filed Amended Statement of Defence dated 8th July 2014 on 14th July 2014.
Claimant filed Amended Reply to Defendant's Statement of Defence dated and filed on 28th October 2015.
Trial commenced on 5th November 2015 with claimant testifying as CW, adopting written statement on oath marked Exhibit C1 and tendering 13 other exhibits.
Defendant called one witness, Eriba Eyenmi.

material_facts: Claimant was employed by the defendant in 1982 and retired in 1996.
Claimant contends he retired with the rank of Assistant Security Officer (ASO).
Defendant contends claimant retired with the rank of Chief Detective (CD).
Claimant avers he was not paid his full monthly pension and commenced this action.
Defendant avers claimant was involved in Orderly Room trial for misconduct in 1994 and received punishment of severe reprimand which affected his promotion.
Defendant avers claimant rose to rank of Chief Detective on 1st January 1994 and was compulsorily retired with effect from 5th March 1996.
Defendant avers letter of retirement Ref. No. C200/32/T dated 5th March 1996 addressing claimant as ASO is erroneous and never emanated from defendant.
Defendant avers claimant's computerized arrears stood at #403,982.20 and monthly pension is #11,317.77.
Claimant avers he was exonerated from blame in Orderly Room trial and retired with clean record.
Claimant avers his promotion to ASO depended on achievements and performance during service.

chronology.event: Claimant involved in Orderly Room trial for misconduct; promoted to Chief Detective on 1st January 1994.
Suit commenced in Federal High Court Uyo.

admitted_facts: Claimant was employed by defendant in 1982.
Claimant receives a monthly pension from defendant.
disputed_facts: Whether claimant retired with the rank of Assistant Security Officer (ASO) or Chief Detective (CD).
Whether claimant was underpaid his pension.
Whether the letter of retirement Ref. No. C200/32/T dated 5th March 1996 was issued by defendant.
Whether claimant was promoted to ASO.
background_facts: Claimant was employed by defendant in 1982 and retired in 1996.
Claimant contends he retired with the rank of Assistant Security Officer (ASO).
Defendant contends claimant retired with the rank of Chief Detective (CD).
facts.employment_relationship: Claimant was an employee of the defendant from 1982 until his retirement in 1996.
facts.contractual_relationship: Employment relationship governed by terms of service of the Department of State Service.
documentary_evidence: Exhibit C1: Claimant's written statement on oath.
Exhibit C3: Letter of retirement from service Ref. No. C200/32/T dated 5th March 1996.
Exhibit C4: Circular No. B63216/S.1/13/105 of 20th January 1997.
Exhibit C5: Circular No. S.1549/10 of 23rd February 2001.
Exhibit C6: Letter from defendants to claimant dated 20th October 1993.
Exhibit C7-C7(5): Six letters from defendants to different persons dated 23rd February 2001.
Exhibit C8: Letter from defendants dated 15th July 2013 to Association of Retired Officers.
Exhibit C9: Letter from National Pension Commission to Daniel & Daniel Attorneys.
Exhibit C10: Certified true copy of Circular Ref SWC/S/04/S.08/Vol. IV/207 of 5th August 2010.
Exhibit C11: Photocopy of government circular B.63216/S.1/X/840 of 5th October 2000.
Exhibit C12: Letter written by claimant to defendants on 13th March 2008.
Exhibit C14: Computer generated Bank Statement of Accounts.
witness_evidence: Claimant testified as CW and adopted his written statement on oath.
Defendant called one witness, Eriba Eyenmi, of the defendant's Personnel Department.

claims.claim: Declaration that it is wrongful, unlawful and unconstitutional for the defendant to discriminate against the claimant by not paying him a monthly pension of #40,638.93 but pays a smaller amount of #13,792.10 contrary to periodical increments done by the Federal Government of Nigeria for retired Federal workers.
Order directing the defendant to pay the claimant the sum of #4,318,642.46 representing unpaid arrears of pension from 1999 till September, 2013.
Exemplary damages of #5,000,000.00 against the defendant.
#1,700,000.00 being the cost of this suit.

reliefs_sought.relief: A DECLARATION that it is wrongful, unlawful and unconstitutional for the defendant to discriminate against the claimant by not paying him a monthly pension of #40,638.93 but pays a smaller amount of #13,792.10 contrary to periodical increments done by the Federal Government of Nigeria for the retired Federal workers.

AN ORDER of Court directing the defendant to pay the claimant the sum of #4,318,642.46 (Four Million, Three Hundred and Eighteen Thousand, Six Hundred and Forty Two Naira, Forty Six Kobo) only which represents the unpaid arrears of pension accruable to the claimant from 1999 till September, 2013.
Exemplary damages of #5,000,000.00 (Five Million Naira) against the defendant.
#1,700,000.00 being the cost of this suit.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether based on the available facts and evidence before this Honorable Court the claimant is entitled to his reliefs.
Whether the suit of the claimant is competent in view of the Limitation Law i.e. Sec. 2 (a) of the Public Officers Protection Act, LFN, 2004.

questions_of_law: Whether the suit is statute barred under Section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act.
Whether the claimant has proved entitlement to pension as an Assistant Security Officer.

claimant_arguments: Claimant is entitled to his reliefs as he has proved his case by adducing credible evidence.
It is not necessary to tender the letter of promotion as the letter of retirement is sufficient.
The defendant ought to have tendered the letter of clearance because payment of entitlements depended upon issuance of clearance letter.
Exhibit C5 is an original private document and Exhibit C11 contains useful private documents that will assist the Court.
The case is competent and not affected by the Public Officers Protection Act as the cause of action bothers on debt.
Claimant retired as an ASO and is entitled to be paid #40,638.13 as monthly pension.
The defendant has not entered appearance in this case.
The defendant's address filed on 2nd August, 2016 is incompetent for non-compliance with Rule 10 of Professional Conduct for Legal Practitioners, 2007.
defendant_arguments: Claimant is not entitled to the reliefs sought as he who asserts must prove his case with credible and unchallenged evidence.
Declaratory relief falls within the discretionary power of the Court.
Claimant ought to have called the maker of Exhibit C3 as a witness.
Exhibits C4, C5, C7, C9, C10, C11 & C12 are public documents that require certification before admission into evidence.
Exhibit C14 is a computer generated document that did not comply with Section 84 of the Evidence Act, 2011.
Claimant has not led any evidence in proof of the claim that his alleged non-payment has infringed on his constitutional rights.
The suit is statute barred under Section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act as the cause of action arose in 1999.
The defendant is not indebted to the claimant in any way.

party_authorities.proposition: He who asserts must prove his case with credible and unchallenged evidence.
Party who wishes to succeed must adduce credible evidence to establish his case.

party_authorities.authority: Section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Act, LFN, 2004

Compliance with constitutional provisions for periodical increments of monthly pensions.

party_authorities.proposition: Cause of action in this case bothers on debt.

evidential_findings.finding: Insufficient to establish that claimant was promoted to ASO.

findings_of_fact.finding: Claimant did not provide evidence of promotion to ASO; defendant's contention that he retired as Chief Detective is more credible.
Claimant failed to provide evidence of what the ASO pension was or that he was entitled to it.

findings_of_law.finding: The suit is not statute barred because the cause of action is continuing injury (periodic pension payments).
The court may depart from the Evidence Act in the interest of justice; Exhibit C14 remains admitted.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court found that the claimant failed to establish the fundamental basis of his claim, specifically that he was promoted to ASO. The letter of retirement alone was insufficient. The court also found that the suit was not statute barred due to continuing injury. The court dismissed the suit.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether based on the available facts and evidence before this Honorable Court the claimant is entitled to his reliefs.

arguments.claimant: Claimant argued he was entitled to reliefs as he proved his case and retired as ASO.
arguments.defendant: Defendant argued claimant failed to prove his case and was not entitled to reliefs.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that the claimant failed to prove that he was promoted to ASO. The letter of retirement alone was insufficient. The claimant also failed to provide evidence of the pension entitlement of an ASO.
issue_analysis.holding: Claimant is not entitled to the reliefs sought.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A claimant must prove the basis of his claim; mere assertion without evidence is insufficient.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether the suit of the claimant is competent in view of the Limitation Law i.e. Sec. 2 (a) of the Public Officers Protection Act, LFN, 2004.

arguments.claimant: Claimant argued the suit is competent and not affected by the Public Officers Protection Act as the cause of action is debt.
arguments.defendant: Defendant argued the suit is statute barred as the cause of action arose in 1999.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that the cause of action is underpayment of pension, which is a continuing injury, and thus falls within the exception to the limitation law.
issue_analysis.holding: The suit is not statute barred.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: For the exception of continuance of damage or injury to apply, there must be periodicity of payment, such as monthly pension.

holdings.holding: Claimant failed to prove entitlement to reliefs.

ratio_decidendi.principle: Promotion in employment law is a factual situation that cannot be inferred or attributed; it must be proved.
ratio_decidendi.application: Claimant failed to prove he was promoted to ASO.

ratio_decidendi.principle: The exception of continuance of damage or injury to limitation law applies where there is periodicity of payment, such as monthly pension.
ratio_decidendi.application: Claimant's pension is paid monthly, so the suit is not statute barred.
